body:
WHAT
Grep runs the bundled ripgrep binary (@vscode/ripgrep) over the workspace. It supports three output modes (files_with_matches, content, count), -i, -n, -A/-B/-C context, glob and type filters, multiline, and head_limit (default 250 lines). It respects .gitignore. ripgrep exit code 1 means no matches and is returned as 'No matches found.', not an error; a result larger than the 20MB buffer is returned truncated with a note instead of failing.

WHY
Without correct exit-code mapping every empty search would look like a failure to the agent; without the buffer handling a broad search would throw away all matches.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/grep.ts — grepTool (permissionClass 'read', searchTerms), execute(): argument building per output_mode, execFile(rgPath, args, { maxBuffer: 20MB, signal }), the ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER branch, code 0 with head_limit truncation suffix, code 1 -> 'No matches found.', other codes -> 'ripgrep error:' with isError.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a temp dir with a.txt 'hello' and b.txt 'world', run Grep { pattern:'zzz' }; assert content 'No matches found.' and isError undefined (exit code 1 path).
2. Run Grep { pattern:'hello', output_mode:'content' }; assert the content contains 'a.txt' and '1:hello' (line numbers on by default) and not 'b.txt'; with output_mode 'count' assert 'a.txt:1'.
3. Run Grep { pattern:'[' } (invalid regex); assert isError:true and content starts with 'ripgrep error:'.
4. Create a file with 1000 matching lines and run with head_limit 10 in content mode; assert 10 result lines plus a '[truncated — ... more lines' suffix.
5. Simulate the maxBuffer path by generating a file with more than 20MB of matching lines (or by monkeypatching execFile to call back with err.code 'ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER' and partial stdout); assert the result is not an error and ends with 'output exceeded the 20MB buffer'.
